title: STARTbeforeCORT randomized controlled multicenter trial – STArt Respiratory sTabilization BEFORE umbilical CORd Transfusion (SBC) in extremely preterm infants: a randomized controlled multicentre trial of safety and efficiency
summary: In extremely preterm infants, this study investigates whether starting respiratory stabilization before umbilical cord clamping (SBC) improves survival without major morbidity compared to standard delayed cord clamping (DCC). The trial will be conducted at up to ten centers in Germany.
conditions: Extreme prematurity (gestational age 22+0–27+6 weeks) with risk for major neonatal morbidities (IVH, BPD, NEC, ROP, cPVL).

interventions.name: STARTbeforeCORT (SBC): Start of respiratory stabilization before umbilical cord transfusion in preterm infants 22+0–27+6 weeks’ gestation.
Delayed Cord Clamping (DCC): Delayed clamping of the umbilical cord 30–60 seconds after birth according to clinical standard.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Preterm infants born between 22+0 and 27+6 weeks’ gestation
Birth till max. 1 hour after birth (time window for study inclusion)
Written informed consent of parents or legal guardian
Exclusion criteria:
Spontaneous vaginal delivery
Emergency delivery with insufficient time for informed consent
Non-lastborn multiple
Severe congenital malformations (neurological, pulmonary, cardiac)
Decision for palliative care only
Parents unable to understand study information due to language barriers
